title: Stabilizer-preserving etale local finite flat affine covers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, stacks in groupoids, and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$. Define $I_{\mathcal X}(T)$ to have objects $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$, and arrows $a:(x,\alpha)\to(y,\beta)$ satisfying $a\alpha=\beta a$. Assume $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ is finite, meaning every scheme base change is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A finite flat affine cover of a stack $\mathcal A$ means an affine scheme $U$ and a representable surjective morphism $U\to\mathcal A$ which is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, tested after scheme base change using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of stacks is separated when its relative diagonal is proper, with properness tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-proper-morphism]. There is a set-indexed family $g_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$ of representable separated etale morphisms whose images jointly cover $|\mathcal X|$, where each $\mathcal X_i$ is Deligne--Mumford and admits a finite flat affine cover, and for every $T$ and $x\in\mathcal X_i(T)$ the map of automorphism sheaves $\operatorname{Aut}_T(x)\to\operatorname{Aut}_T(g_i x)$ is an isomorphism. Equivalently, $I_{\mathcal X_i}\to\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X}$ is an isomorphism. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts. Here $|\mathcal X|$ consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension.

proof.text: Fix $x\in|\mathcal X|$. Apply the pointed finite-groupoid neighbourhood theorem to obtain $g:\mathcal Q=[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ and $q$ over $x$. Here $U,R$ are affine, the projections $s,t$ are finite locally free, and $g$ is representable etale and is an isomorphism on the geometric stabilizer at $q$. This step uses only preservation at this one point, not preservation on the entire neighbourhood.

Apply the stabilizer-isomorphism open-locus theorem to $g$, using precisely the finite inertia of its target $\mathcal X$. It gives an open $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal Q$ containing $q$, with $I_{\mathcal V}\simeq\mathcal V\times_{\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X}$. By finite-flat quotient geometry its inverse image $V=U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal V$ is an invariant open of $U$. The surjectivity of $|U|\to|\mathcal Q|$ supplies $v\in V$ mapping to $q$. Its orbit $E=t(s^{-1}(\{v\}))$ is a finite set, contains $v$, and lies in $V$: finiteness is the finite-fibre clause of finite locally free, and invariance of $V$ puts both endpoints of each such arrow in $V$.

Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $J\subseteq A$ cut out the closed complement $U\setminus V$. For each $e\in E$, the prime $\mathfrak p_e$ does not contain $J$. Prime avoidance gives $a\in J$ outside every $\mathfrak p_e$, so $E\subseteq D(a)\subseteq V$ and $D(a)$ is affine. Since $V$ is invariant, the groupoid restricted to $V$ has finite locally free projections by the quotient-geometry lemma. Apply the existing invariant-affine-neighbourhood lemma to this restricted groupoid and $v$, with the affine open $D(a)$ containing its orbit. Obtain an invariant affine open $W\subseteq V$ containing $v$. No affineness of $V$ or of intersections of arbitrary affine opens is assumed.

Invariance inside $V$ is also invariance in $U$, since $V$ was invariant. Finite-flat quotient geometry therefore gives the open substack $\mathcal W=[W/R_W]\subseteq\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal Q$. It contains $q$ and admits the required finite flat affine cover $W\to\mathcal W$. It is absolutely separated because $W$ is affine. By representable etale calculus, restriction of $g$ gives a representable etale map $g_x:\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$. The source is Deligne--Mumford: base-change an etale scheme atlas of $\mathcal Q$ to the open substack, obtaining an etale scheme atlas of $\mathcal W$.

The separated-source cancellation theorem applies to $g_x$: its source $\mathcal W$ is absolutely separated and its target $\mathcal X$ has finite inertia. Thus $g_x$ is separated. On the strictly full open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal V$, the inertia comparison is the restriction of the isomorphism from step 2: for an object $w$ and any automorphism of $g_x(w)$, that isomorphism gives a unique automorphism of $w$ in $\mathcal V$, which is also in $\mathcal W$ by fullness. This proves the stated automorphism-sheaf isomorphism on every test scheme, hence the inertia isomorphism.

The construction works for every $x\in|\mathcal X|$ and produces $q\in|\mathcal W|$ with $g_x(q)=x$. Using the stated universe bound, choose one construction for each point of the set $|\mathcal X|$. Their images cover by this equality, and every chosen map has all properties established in steps 1--5. If $|\mathcal X|$ is empty take the empty family.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q77-c5f7760b1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks 0DUE in full (statement and proof) and the tags behind it: 0DUL/0DUM, 0DU4, 0DUA, 050M(3) and 0CL0(1). The item statement is unchanged; it is 0DUE restricted to DM stacks over an arbitrary scheme base S, with nothing weakened. Steps: (1) the pointed node gives a stabilizer isomorphism only at q, as 0DU4 does; (2) the 0DUA locus gives V, which is invariant and contains q, and the orbit E is finite and lies in V because s is finite and V is invariant; (3) prime avoidance applies because E is nonempty, giving E ⊆ D(a) ⊆ V, and 03JE applied to (V,R_V) gives an invariant affine W; (4) the quotient-geometry node gives [W/R_W] with a finite flat cover, absolute separatedness by implicitly applying its last clause to (W,R_W), and DM by restricting the atlas, while the étale calculus gives the restriction of g; (5) cancellation gives separatedness, and the inertia isomorphism restricts to the full substack; (6) choice over the set |X|, with the empty case covered. New nodes: all four are true and statement-only, none restates a clause of the item, and each was tested on schemes, BG with p dividing |G|, and a non-separated S. In quotient geometry I checked that p is finite and representable by schemes, the invariant-open bijection, and that R → U×_Z U is finite, hence proper, so the quotient is absolutely separated even over a non-separated S. No duplicates in snapshot, live or side-live: the field-base 0DUE sibling lem-sfb-finite-inertia-etale-affine-charts does not supply the item; invariant-open-substack-descent needs a smooth atlas, flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient gives no finiteness, opens or separatedness, and separation-composition is 050K, not cancellation. lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_inertia_local_affine_covers {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hX : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack X) (hfinite : IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap (moduliInertiaProjection X)) : ∃ (I : Type (max (u + 1) w)) (A : I → BasedCategory.{max u v, max (u + 1) w} (Over S)) (g : ∀ i : I, BasedFunctor (A i) X), (∀ i : I, IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack (A i) ∧ IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (g i) ∧ IsEtaleModuliMap (g i) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) X) (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange (g i) T t Z a → AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsProper f.left) (pullback.diagonal a)) ∧ (∃ (U : Over S) (_ : IsAffine U.left) (p : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) (A i)), ModuliSchemeTest (fun _ _ f ↦ IsFinite f ∧ Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ Surjective f) p) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (x : Functor.Fiber (A i).p T), Function.Bijective (fun α : x ≅ x ↦ (moduliFiberMap (g i) T).mapIso α))) ∧ ∀ x : ModuliPoints X, ∃ (i : I) (y : ModuliPoints (A i)), moduliPointMap (g i) y = x
